kitDescription: Ade is a Wind-element Supporter who fires an assault rifle and carries a Burst II skill on a 20-second cooldown. At the start of battle she makes all allies immune to one debuff (stacking once, maintained), and whenever her own HP falls below 90% she grants the whole team an ATK buff equal to 5.19% of her own ATK for 5 seconds. Her second skill refreshes that same debuff immunity after 420 normal attacks, and after every 120 normal attacks she raises all allies' Max HP by 15.62% of her own Max HP for 5 seconds without healing anyone. Her burst raises all allies' Max HP by 25.15% of her Max HP and their ATK by 10.15% of her ATK, both for 10 seconds, again without restoring HP. She contributes no skill or burst damage of her own — her entire offensive value is the two team ATK buffs riding on her rifle normal attacks.

Duration 5s matches prose. Only the trigger is approximated: no HP-threshold primitive exists and the v1 boss deals no damage, so the literal gate cannot be evaluated.
skill1.explanation: RULING ON THE OPEN QUESTION: the driver's encoding is FAITHFUL-as-documented-gap, not a REAL-GOTCHA, and it must NOT be forced back to UNMODELED. The mast precedent governs: an offensive HP-below gate with a missing primitive ships always-on with a measurement-gated flag, and mast's reconciling judge ruled exactly this DOCUMENTED_GAP inside a GO verdict; biscuit's UNMODELED case is distinguishable (defensive invincibility, no damage channel). Ade's 90% threshold is easier to cross than mast's 70%, so the near-full-uptime estimate is if anything stronger, and every agent including S2b agrees the over-credit direction is bounded and measurement-gated. Between the two modeled encodings, the driver's interval:5 is strictly more faithful than S6's: S6's passive + durationSec 5 under the fused-passive semantics (sim.ts ~2179) applies once at frame 0 and expires at t=5s, never re-applying — covering 5 of 180 seconds and contradicting S6's own 'always-on' caveat. That is a blind-side engine-semantics misread (a RECON_ERROR-grade divergence on S6's artifact), not corroboration of any driver defect; the driver's refresh keeps the kit's 5s window continuously live from t=5s. The divergence is fully documented on both sides (⚑2 note + caveats + rejected-alternative record), which is exactly what DOCUMENTED_GAP requires. Residual risk is the mast-identical one — the pre-onset transient and real-fight uptime — and the stated recipe is the correct next step.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs: all six kit lines are either FAITHFUL (skill2 Max HP grant, both burst lines — all three firing at prose cadence and discriminated against their nearest-wrong models) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (the two Perfect Maid immunity lines recorded verbatim with reasons, and the S1 HP<90% ATK gate shipped always-on under the mast GO-1.0 precedent with ⚑2 estimate + recipe + tier and S2b's UNMODELED logged as the rejected alternative). The blind re-derivations converged on everything except the one arbitrated line: S5's intent-preserved assertions run 15/15 green + 2 intentional GAP skips against the shipped override (its original file's 12 reds were all blind-internal wiring bugs B1–B5 — onEvent placement, OverrideFile shape, the crown-slot-priority fixture starvation, 5-vs-4 comp size, and the basis-invariant self-total comparison — each a RECON_ERROR, none a driver divergence), and S6's override is byte-identical to the driver's on skill2/burst/unmodeled. On the HP-gate line the driver's interval:5 refresh is the strongest of the three positions: S2b's UNMODELED is defensible but loses to the mast precedent for an offensive gate, and S6's passive + durationSec 5 contradicts its own 'always-on' caveat under the engine's fused-passive semantics (live t∈[0,5] only, never re-applies) — a blind-side engine-semantics misread, not corroboration of any driver defect. The same-model residual the owner should spot-check: every agent in this gauntlet converged on MODELED for the HP gate, and same-family convergence proves stability, not correctness — the ⚑2 recipe (HP-bar crossing time + buff-icon uptime from an ade focus video) is the one measurement that could still move this line, in either direction (a healer comp keeping ade above 90% would make even UNMODELED optimistic relative to always-on). Minor doc nit, not a finding: the shipped override note names 'liter/ade/crown/ada/helm' as the co-B2 comp while the test correctly uses biscuit (40s CD) after the test's own comment explains crown (20s CD) never splits stage 2 under liter's CDR — worth a one-line note cleanup, no behavioral impact. Nothing must change for GO.
